name: Monport GM Pro MOPA
tagline: Compact all-in-one JPT MOPA fiber with autofocus, in 30W and 60W
tldr: The GM Pro MOPA is Monport's integrated fiber with a JPT MOPA source: the pulse adjusts from 2 to 500 ns and the frequency from 1 to 4,000 kHz, which opens colour marking on stainless steel and titanium and cleaner black marks on aluminum. One-touch autofocus, electric lift and a 175 × 175 mm field on both tiers: 30W ($2,978) and 60W ($3,598) in October 2026. Open a tier for exact specs.
mainObjective: Colour marking and fine metal engraving from a compact one-piece fiber

priceRange.note: Official Monport store, Oct 2026: 30W MOPA $2,978, 60W MOPA $3,598; the LightBurn Pro bundle adds $200, the rotary bundle $150. A manual-focus GM 60W MOPA is listed at $3,500

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

cutExample.description: Not a sheet cutter: thin metal only, in many passes

cannot: Clear glass or acrylic marking (needs UV or CO₂)
Parts larger than the 175 × 175 mm field without repositioning

pros: JPT MOPA sources with 2–500 ns pulse control: colour on stainless steel and titanium, black marks on aluminum
Autofocus, electric lift and a 175 × 175 mm field on both tiers
Hundreds of dollars below Monport's split MOPA machines at the same power
cons: Open galvo with a Class 4 beam: an enclosure or strict eye protection is required
Colour marking takes test grids and patience: results depend on alloy and surface
400 mm maximum Z height, less than Monport's split GT series

faq.question: Which GM Pro MOPA tier should I choose?
faq.answer: The 30W ($2,978) handles colour marking, black marking on aluminum and plastics well. The 60W ($3,598) doubles the pulse energy (2 mJ vs 1 mJ), which matters for deep engraving, relief and thin-sheet cutting. Both share the field, chassis and autofocus.

faq.question: How does the GM Pro MOPA compare with Monport's GT 60W MOPA?
faq.answer: The GT is a split fiber with a separate source cabinet, a 550 mm Z height and an autofocus version listed at $4,270. The GM Pro 60W MOPA keeps autofocus and the same 175 × 175 mm field in a one-piece chassis for $3,598 (October 2026).

standoutFeatures.title: Colour marking in a compact chassis
standoutFeatures.body: Adjustable pulse width from 2 to 500 ns and frequency up to 4,000 kHz give controlled oxide colours on stainless steel and titanium from a machine that fits on a 40 × 33 cm footprint.

standoutFeatures.title: Larger field than the GM Pro
standoutFeatures.body: Both MOPA tiers use a 175 × 175 mm field, against 150 × 150 mm on the standard GM Pro, with the same autofocus and electric lift.

beginnerNotes: This overview covers the GM Pro MOPA line. Choose the 30W for colour and fine marking on a budget, the 60W when depth and speed also count. For plain marking without colour, the standard GM Pro costs less.
proTips: Build colour test grids on your own alloy before quoting colour jobs, and keep notes of speed, frequency and pulse settings: colours shift with surface finish.
primaryUse: Integrated MOPA fiber laser for colour marking and metal engraving.

editorialDepth.advantages: The GM Pro MOPA brings MOPA colour marking and autofocus to a one-piece fiber priced well below split MOPA machines, a good fit for jewelry, gifts and anodized aluminum work.
editorialDepth.limitations: The open galvo needs an enclosure or strict eye protection, colour work has a learning curve, and the specs are Monport's until independent reviews appear.
